maker: Bell sec., Christian Wittmann, Nuremberg; slide sec., Nuremberg manuf., ca. 1740.¹
signature: "C W Nürnberg"; maker's mark: circle with six-pointed star and initials "C" and "W"; imperial coat of arms; owner's mark in plate, applied at later date, with initials "I S."
pitch: B$ at a = 438; built in B% Cammerton.
mouthpiece: Perhaps from a tenorhorn(?); cf. Heyde 1980a: 198, 202, tafel 16, 26.
remarks: Loud, somewhat harsh sound.7 pos.; bell at 4th pos.; Nuremberg-style rim-wire; plant ornaments on flat bell-stay; tubular slide-stays; ring in slide-bow, bell-bow; except for soldered bell-stay, no substantial repairs; bell sec. much plainer than Nuremberg trombones of mid-18th century, with little decoration; slide sec. perhaps from circle of Johann Leonard Ehe III; Heyde thinks Wittmann may have taken over the workshop of Martin Friedrich Ehe.
